notes.note: State of a job that was cancelled after some of its steps had run: the cancellation undid those steps.
Manual undo task for a step that cannot be undone automatically. The argument step is the step number, name the short name of the step, such as "Reserve in DHCP".

segment.source: Undo step {step} ({name}) by hand, then mark this done.

notes.note: Heading of the list of jobs in a job group that ended without their change (rolled back, failed or cancelled).
Explains the "Not moved" list of a job group. move-failed is a tag value and stays as it is.

segment.source: These jobs ended without their change. A moved object keeps its old address and carries the tag move-failed until its next successful move.

notes.note: Shown in the "Not moved" list when the job recorded no error.
State of a job in the jobs list while a task of it waits for a person to do or confirm it.
Column header of the jobs list: how many steps of the job are done, or for a job that is done how long it took.
The Steps cell of a job in the jobs list: done is the number of steps done, total the number of steps of the job.
How long a job took when it took less than a second.
Tooltip of the duration of a job that is done; duration reads like "2 min 10 s".
Group row at the top of the jobs list: the jobs with a task that waits for a person.
Group row of the jobs list: the jobs that are queued, running, rolling back or waiting for the network.
Group row of the jobs list: the jobs that finished today.
Group row of the jobs list: the jobs that finished yesterday.
Group row of the jobs list: the jobs that finished before yesterday.

After the count of a day group of the jobs list, as in "Today · 12 done". outcome is done when every job of the day succeeded, failed when every one failed or was rolled back, mixed when some did, other otherwise (some were cancelled); failed is the number that failed or were rolled back.

segment.source: {outcome, select, done {done} failed {failed or rolled back} mixed {finished, {failed, number} failed or rolled back} other {finished}}

notes.note: Last row of the Today group of the jobs list when it shows only its first ten jobs; count is how many more there are.

segment.source: Show the rest of today ({count, number} more)

notes.note: Last row of the Yesterday group of the jobs list when it shows only its first ten jobs; count is how many more there are.

segment.source: Show the rest of yesterday ({count, number} more)

notes.note: Last row of the Earlier group of the jobs list when it shows only its first ten jobs; count is how many more there are.

segment.source: Show the rest of the earlier jobs ({count, number} more)

notes.note: Last row of the oldest day group of the jobs list when the server has older finished jobs than the ones read.

The line of facts under the title of the jobs list. running is the number of jobs that run, waiting the number that wait for a person (the number of the Jobs badge in the navigation), finished the number of finished jobs read, such as 200+.

segment.source: {running, number} running · {waiting, number} waiting for you · {finished} finished

notes.note: The line of facts under the title of the jobs list when the number of jobs that wait for a person is not known. finished is the number of finished jobs read, such as 200+.
The one line above the finished jobs when no job runs and none waits for a person.

segment.source: Nothing is running and no job waits for you. Finished jobs are below.

notes.note: Said once in the filter bar of the jobs list when one person started every listed job, instead of a Started by column. who is that person, or the word for "you".
The argument who of "Started by · all {who}" when the signed-in user started every listed job.
